title: Google Review Cards For Auto Dealerships
summary: This guide helps auto dealerships deploy Google review cards across sales and service locations by focusing on branch routing, handoff timing and whether the prompt belongs at the desk, delivery point or service pickup counter.
heroPoints: Dealership review prompts often split between sales delivery and service handoff moments.
Branch routing needs to be stable before a group starts printing several store batches.
The strongest pilot tests one sales-side and one service-side workflow before scaling.
imageAlt: Google review card planning for auto dealerships

sections.title: What this guide covers
sections.intro: Use this guide when the project already knows the use case, but still needs a tighter implementation or validation workflow before requesting samples or pricing.
bullets: How dealer groups separate sales, service and pickup workflows before choosing the review format.
Why branch-level routing and location ownership matter before group printing starts.
What to validate in a pilot before rolling review prompts out to multiple rooftops.

sections.title: Recommended workflow
sections.intro: These steps keep the first sample or deployment round focused on the questions that change the buying decision most.
bullets: Map each dealership location and separate sales delivery from service pickup or cashier moments.
Choose whether the prompt is staff-delivered, fixed on a counter or split by department.
Pilot one representative store and one representative department mix before wider printing.
Scale only after routing, handoff behavior and reorder needs are clear enough to support the network.

sections.title: Common mistakes to avoid
sections.intro: These are the patterns that often slow down projects because the team moves into samples or pricing before the core workflow is clear enough.
bullets: Using one generic rollout plan for both sales delivery and service pickup.
Approving multi-store print before confirming which location or department each prompt should route to.
Treating the format decision as purely visual when desk flow and handoff timing are the real blockers.

faq.question: Should dealerships use one review-card setup for sales and service?
faq.answer: Not always. Sales delivery and service pickup often create different handoff moments, so the routing and physical format may need to differ even within one store.

faq.question: What should a dealership pilot prove first?
faq.answer: It should prove branch routing, department-level placement and whether the handoff actually fits sales and service workflow before a broader group rollout begins.
